r.name: P09 - Cicogna - Ponte Velina
r.description: Between ancient summer pastures and centuries-old chestnut to explore the southern part of the National Park to reach the last inhabited permanently pasture of the Val Grande

r.name: P00 - Madonna di Campagna - Santino - Rovegro- Cossogno- Cicogna - Pogallo
P07a - Cappella Or Vergugn - Ponte Velina
r.description: From the Or Vegugn Chapel, on the path P07, to Velina Bridge, to the cross with P50 path along the river, through Alpe Bettina. You enter the wild Valgrande following the old path used to load the Velina Alps starting from Rovegro

r.name: XP1A - Ponte Casletto - Ponte Velina
r.description: A daring and challenging route that runs along the steep side of the Rio Valgrande with frequent dripping tunnels where an open-air water conduit flows, dilapidated small bridge and a Tibetan Bridge are the final highlight.

r.name: P50b - Orfalecchio - Val Foiera - Corte Buè
r.description: Alternative route to leave or reach the Ferrata Selvaggio Verde with views over the entire Valgrande. It runs for a stretch along the line of the old cableway for timber of which the pylons remain

r.name: X01 - La strà di vacch
r.description: The cows reached the pastures of Orfalecchio and Rodugno starting from Rovegro following this historic road. Today it is partially included in the Riserva naturale integrata del Pedum and therefore the access is forbidden in that section

r.name: X06 - Orfalecchio - Alpe Rodugno - Bocchetta di Saltir
r.description: From Orfalecchio with steep climb to Alpe Rodugno and then on mountain side below the ridge of the Corni di Nibbio you reach the Bocchetta di Sautir

r.name: P12 - Pogallo - Bocchetta di Terza
r.description: From Val Pogallo to Val Cannobina, crossing the ridge where the Bove path runs. This was also the route of the partisans fleeing to Switzerland during the German-Fascist raid of 1944

r.name: P08 - Cicogna -Tregugno - la Soliva - Pian Cavallone
r.description: A challenging path for complexity, development and difficulty, the path from la Soliva to the Forcola Saddle is on steep meadows and You crosse a valley with vertical rocky walls supported by the chains

r.name: SENTIERO BOVE - 1A TAPPA da Cicogna a Pian Cavallone
r.description: Tough route for steep slopes to go up, but no technical difficulty, even marks, albeit sometimes distant, are present throughout the path and the trace is always visible

r.name: SENTIERO BOVE - 6A TAPPA da Bivacco Bta di Campo a Cicogna via Cima Sasso
r.description: The Strette del Casè range from the Bocchetta di Campo to the Prati di Ghina. Here we continue with a challenging ridge's path to Cima Sasso. From the Prati di Ghina you can reach Pogallo with the easiest route to Cavrua

r.name: X07SN - Strette del Casè via Cima Sasso da Sud a Nord
r.description: It is less tiring and simpler to travel the Strette from North to South: see X07NS, here we present the route from South to North, from Cima Sasso to Bocchetta di Campo. We refer to the X07NS path for the information common to both

r.name: In bici tra i fiumi
r.description: Il nome del percorso è collegato ai cinque fiumi toccati lungo l'itinerario: Toce, Bogna, Diveria, Isorno e Melezzo. Il percorso è segnalato con frecce azzurre e deve essere obbligatoriamente effettuato in SENSO ORARIO.

r.name: SENTIERO BOVE - 4A TAPPA da Bivacco Lidesh a Bivacco Scaredi
r.description: One of the most challenging stages of the Bove trail, the ascent to the Torrione on the Passo delle Crocette side is mountaineering and facilitated by chains, the ascent on the Bocchetta di Terza side is all on a trail with very exposed sections

r.name: L00 - Da Altoggio alla Bocchetta del Lago Gelato
A04 - Pontetto - Cappella della Croce
r.description: Very long and challenging route with exposed sections, The first part crosses the villages of Montecrestese in the second the mountain pastures that surround Mount Larone, a panoramic stretch halfway up the hillside.

r.name: SENTIERO BOVE - 5A TAPPA da Bivacco Scaredi a Bivacco Bta di Campo
r.description: A short stage along the scenic ridge that marks the northern border of the Pogallo Valley, which extends between Cima della Laurasca and Pedum. This stage approaches the feared Strette del Casè.

r.name: M14 - Malesco - Bocchetta di Cortechiuso
r.description: From Malesco to Fondo li Gabbi in Val Loana, partially following the road and then for mule track at Alpe Scaredi gate of the Val Grande, then with easy path, in the high meadows, to the Bocchetta di Cortechiuso

r.name: P17 - Bivio M14 presso Cima della Laurasca - Rifugio Bta di Campo
r.description: Path access to the Rifugio Bocchetta Campo and part of the BOVE trail. It winds on the north side of the Cima della Laurasca and then on the ridge between Val Pogallo and Valle Aperta

r.name: P40 - Alpe in La Piana - Alpe della Colma
r.description: Final path of the classic North South crossing of the wild Valgrande for a route easy to follow and maintained by the Ente Parco Valgrande

r.name: A40 - Premosello - Pizzo Proman
r.description: Itinerary with a difference in height of 1900m starting from Premosello Chiovenda, but by car it is possible to climb up almost to the Alpe La Piana on a paved road, saving 800 meters of slope
Sentiero Italia - Tappa E58

r.name: P14 - Pogallo - Cima Marsicce
r.description: A magnificent panoramic path with breathtaking views of the ridges of the BOVE trail, elementary but tiring to the Alpe Busarasca, the long final crest is reserved for hikers specially experienced

r.name: P06 - Cicogna - Varola - Curgei - Pizzo Pernice
r.description: Tough route for steep slopes to go up, but no technical difficulty, even marks, albeit sometimes distant, are present throughout the path and the trace is always visible

r.name: P11 - Cicogna - Cima Sasso
r.description: Panoramic ridge path between Val Pogallo and Val Grande, easy (T) until the Casa dell'Alpino, some little difficulty the final climb to the top (E)

r.name: SENTIERO BOVE - ALTERNATIVA da Strette del Casè a Cicogna via Cavrua
r.description: From the Prati di Ghina (Strette del Casè) to the Alpe Cavrua and Pogallo as far as Cicogna, this is an easier route than the overcoming of Cima Sasso, but the path search difficulties are superior

r.name: X7NS - Strette del Casè via Cima Sasso da Nord a Sud
r.description: The Strette del Casè range from the Bocchetta di Campo to the Prati di Ghina. Here we continue with a challenging ridge's path to Cima Sasso. From the Prati di Ghina you can reach Pogallo with the easiest route to Cavrua

r.name: P13 - Alpe Pogallo - Alpe Leciurt
r.description: With this path you can take a ring from Cicogna to the Casa dell'Alpino (P11) then to the alpi Leciurt, Braco and Caslù to Pogallo (P13) and return to Cicogna on the P00 classic route. Ring not recommended in the opposite direction

r.name: A60 - Linea Cadorna Cuzzago
r.description: Short and easy path along one of the streets Cadorna, defense lines built in the 1915-18 war, with well-preserved trenches and casemates

r.name: P30 - Alpe in La Piana - Alpe Scaredi
r.description: One of the pats of the classic North South crossing of the wild Valgrande for a route easy to follow and maintained by the Ente Parco Valgrande

r.name: Percorso Druogno-Re "Pineta"
r.description: Si tratta dell’itinerario ciclabile per eccellenza della Val Vigezzo in quanto presenta una pista ciclabile dedicata pressoché continua, tranne un breve tratto su strada secondaria a basso traffico prima del campo sportivo di Santa Maria Maggiore e nell’a

r.name: C01 - Villadossola-Alpe Baldana bivio C05
r.description: Route from Villadossola, through the fractions of Piaggio Sopra and Gaggitti, going up, passing through the pastures of Corticcio, Basciumo Sotto and Sopra, reaches the Baldana alp. From here, joning with the path C05, you reach the S. Giacomo alp.

r.name: A53 - Pallanzeno-Alpe Corticcio
r.description: Route from Pallanzeno to Alpe Corticcio passing from the Enel Basin from where you have a nice view of the lower Ossola Valley. From Alpe Corticcio join the path C01 for Basciumo and S. Giacomo

r.name: M19 - Alpe Verzasca - Pioda di Crana
r.description: Well marked path. First part in the forest path not too obvious, then trail ridge also exposed. Steep slopes; last stretch very exposed to avoid in case of rain

r.name: F06 - Varzo - Alpe Solcio
r.description: Well marked trail with several passages next to the road, does not present difficulties

r.name: F02 - Varzo - Alpe Solcio
r.description: Path in the woods, a steep and not always very clean stretch, up to the junction of the Alpe Genuina. Then from there the slopes become less steep, and the path becomes panoramic. F02 always well marked

r.name: F01 - Varzo - Passo Pian Pumper
r.description: Well marked and clean forest path, high marked and evident: lack of water

r.name: In Bici tra i Boschi
r.description: Percorso che attraversa il tratto centrale della valle del Toce, tra campi coltivati e boschi di pianura. Passa nel cuore dell’Oasi Naturalistica WWF Bosco Tenso, un tempo esteso in tutta l’Ossola e ora drasticamente ridotto e frazionato.

r.name: In Bici tra i Borghi
r.description: Percorso che parte da Domodossola, Borgo della Cultura da ammirare nel suo meraviglioso centro storico, e raggiunge l’antica capitale dell’Ossola Inferiore, Vogogna, tra i Borghi più belli d’Italia e Bandiera Arancione dal Touring Club Italiano.

r.name: G00b - Crevoladossola - Oira
r.description: Variant to the Via del Gries which crosses the high villages on the right bank of the Toce river while the Via del Gries remains below near the river

r.name: G00a - Montecrestese - Pontemaglio
r.description: Once a trade route for mule caravans between Switzerland and Italy and called Via dello Sbrinz. There are also megalithic sites nearby. The villages of Lomese and Chezzo are open-air museums worth visiting.

r.name: A00a - Via Francisca (seconda sezione)
r.description: Historical walk along the Francisca Road which takes place mostly on internal roads, mule track and paths. In many crossroads it is difficult to identify the path due to the lack of painted flags and some guideposts

r.name: A00a - Via Francisca (prima sezione)
r.description: Historical walk along the Francisca Road which takes place mostly on internal roads, mule track and paths. In many crossroads it is difficult to identify the path due to the lack of painted flags and some guideposts
Sentiero Italia - Tappa E59
Sentiero Italia - Tappa E66
Sentiero Italia - Tappa E65
Sentiero Italia - Tappa E64

r.name: F50b - Ciamporino - Alpe Solcio
r.description: Superb panoramic half mountainside route, along the path of Alta Via Val Divedro, along pastures still loaded for grazing of cattle with refurbished huts for holiday use where the original features have been maintained.

r.name: A45 - Pieve Vergonte - bivio B97 Alpe Pian Lago
r.description: Percorso impegnativo in ambiente selvaggio a tratti esposto conduce prima ad Alpe Colla e successivamente attraverso traverso agli alpeggi di Ghiaccetto , la Crosa da qui su flebile traccia a tratti esposta si raggiunge il bivio con percorso B97.

r.name: A47 - Fomarco - Pizzo Camino
r.description: A long and strenuous route with challenging sections, especially from Alpe il Ghiaccio onward. But the spectacular views you can enjoy during the climb and from the summit are worth the effort.

r.name: A08 - Masera località Ranco - Alpe Pescia
r.description: Along the ancient mule track of ascent to the mountain pastures. Very scenic route on the Ossolana plain.

r.name: A00 - Strada Romana (prima sezione)
r.description: Historical walk along the Roman Road which takes place mostly on internal roads, mule track and paths. In many crossroads it is difficult to identify the path due to the lack of painted flags and some guideposts

r.name: A22 - Cardezza bivio A00 - Punta della Rossola
r.description: Beautiful mule track to Cardezza, steep and not popular path to Marzone, for Corte di sopra very bumpy and you arrive without a trace. The ridge that climbs to the ridge is among kernels without a trace. However the view from the summit is spectacular

r.name: A00 - Strada Romana (seconda sezione)
r.description: Easy historical walk along the Roman Road which takes place mostly on internal roads, mule track and paths. In many crossroads it is difficult to identify the path due to the lack of painted flags and some guideposts

r.name: M00 - Via del Mercato da Masera a Re (prima sezione)
A40b - bivio A40 - Bocchetta dell'Usciolo
r.description: A very steep and tiring path up to the Alpe Stavelli, beyond a high rocky wall; however suitable for normal hikers for the wide and comfortable track; 10 meters of easy well-stepped rocks are overcome with the help of a recent robust chain

r.name: A03 - Villadossola - Colletto Moncucco
r.description: The path A03 starts from Villadossola and develops on the eastern side of Moncucco up to the hill below the summit, at the junction with path D01 that goes up from Domodossola

r.name: M00a - Via del Mercato (variante per Trontano)
A38 - Premosello - Bocchetta di Saler
r.description: Long and tiring path. It is possible to reduce the height difference by driving up to Colloro. From Premosello to Alpe la Colla it is suitable for normal hikers, besides only expert hikers

r.name: A01 - La Via Alta (Crosiggia - Boschetto)
r.description: The Via Alta - It was the road that connected the valleys, Bognanco and Antrona, without going down to the valley bottom

r.name: D00 - Quarta sezione: Graniga - Monte Calvario
r.description: Fourth section of the Via del Monscera also known as Via Stockalper through villages, gorges, the thermal baths of Bognanco, the Torchio di Monteossolano and the Sacro Monte Calvario

r.name: A03a - Gaggio loc.tà Cavana bivio A03 - bivio con A01 Alpe Maianco inf.
r.description: Path characterized by an alternation of stone steps and very well-made rock passages
Sentiero Italia - Tappa E67

r.name: A34 - Vogogna - Pizzo Lacina
r.description: Very steep and tiring route reserved for expert hikers, the final part is an extremely panoramic ridge over the whole of Ossola

r.name: A32 - Vogogna - Alpe Ceresola - bivio A28
r.description: Steep and tiring route reserved for capable hikers, the final part is an extremely panoramic ridge over the north Ossola

r.name: A20a - bivio A20 presso Beura - Alpe Solia di dentro
r.description: Very steep and tiring path, still well maintained by the Alpigiani di Bissoggio and Solia. Rich in historical interests: the wine press and the bread ovens in Bissoggio, the millstones of Solia and the stone quarries

r.name: G07 - Crodo - Passo della Colmine
r.description: From Crodo to Viceno a nice mule track, crossing several agglomerations. From Viceno to Foppiano the route is no longer marked and in some places difficult to find. The last part from Foppiano to the Pass, a steep route, quite marked and visible.

r.name: H09 - Cravegna - Alpe Agarù. Parte della Veia di Scuettar
r.description: The Veia di Scuettar or Via degli Scoiattoli was once traveled with herds by the inhabitants of Crodo to reach Alpe Devero along a hillside route. To complete it follow H09x and then H09y, the latter very dangerous due to landslide

r.name: A14 - Verigo - Passo di Basagrana
r.description: Mixed route initially through woods and village , in the upper part in abandoned alpine pastures and on wide high altitude basins . We are at the gates of the Val Grande in the national park here fauna and flora abound and make special the route itself

r.name: A16 - Trontano - Passo del Ragozzale
r.description: The route represents one of the historical entrances to Val Grande. It starts from Trontano and passes by the Parpinasca Refuge and Colle di Nava. Then a long half-coast to Alpe Rina and Alpe Menta and then the stone staircase of Ragozzale

r.name: A18 - Quarata di Cosa - Alpe Provo
A18a - Selvaccia bivio A18 - Alpe Cortevecchio bivio A18
A22a - La Strada del Pane da Cuzzego a Cardezza
r.description: An interesting walk along the Strada del Pane where on January 17th Sant'Antonio Abate, bread is carried in procession from Cuzzego to Cardezza. Interesting chapels along the historic paved path

r.name: A24 - Alpe Marzone bivio A22 - Pizzo delle Pecore
r.description: After a long walk on the road, you follow a shady ridge, then a long hillside towards Alpe Cort from which a steep path leads to the panoramic ridge and finally the summit

r.name: A26 - Cuzzego località Carale - bivio A24 Pizzo Colla Bassa
r.description: Tiring and steep path at times made impassable by falling trees, track often not visible, very poor marked, steep and exposed meadows in the upper part

r.name: A28 - Prata - Pizzo Lacina
r.description: Steep and tiring route with very difficult sections to follow, the final part is on extremely steep and trackless meadows. Reserved for very experienced hikers.

r.name: A30 - Vogogna località Dresio - Alpe Marona
A36 - Premosello - bivio A34 Alpe Pianoni
A38a - bivio A38 Colloro - Alpe Lut bivio A40
A17 - Cosa - Pra la Varda
r.description: Unlike many paths of left side of the lower Ossola that are extremely steep and tiring, A17 offers a walk suitable also for tourists up to Cosasca and Madonna delle Grucce, then climbs more difficult to Pra la Varda

r.name: A16b - bivio A16 Alpe Parpinasca - bivio A16 sopra Alpe Drisoni
A44 - Cuzzago - Alpe Vargia
r.description: Route mainly on asphalted road except a first stretch on a slightly bad path, not recommended and avoidable following the road from its beginning

r.name: D05 - Località Torno (quota 443) - Alpe Foppiano (quota 1160)
r.description: path up to Alpe Bei 775 m, then dirt road, to Cascina Vè 996, then with a long traverse in the woods, up to the Domobianca ski slopes

r.name: M24 - Bivio M14 presso Patqueso - La Cima
M14a - Fondo li Gabbi - Le Fornaci
M10 - Malesco loc. Gaia - Bocchetta di Vald
M10f - Alpe Bondolo - Bocchetta di Cavalla
M08 - Santa Maria Maggiore - Rifugio Al Cedo
M02 - Marone - Pizzo Marcio
r.description: Long and tiring route, long unmarked stretches, track sometimes difficult to find and missing in the valley after Sassoledo where there is an elementary rocky jump. Ancient and modern rock engravings in Sassoledo.

r.name: M03 - Coimo - Monte Loccia di Peve
M07 - Sagrogno - Passo della Margina - bivio M03
M09 - Druogno - Monte Mater
r.description: Signposted route. From Sagrogno onwards steep and after Alpe Braghi very steep. First you travel through beech forests and then through coniferous forests until you come out onto the meadows of the very panoramic peak

r.name: M23 - bivio M21 presso San Gerolamo - Bocchetta di Muino
M29a - bivio M27 - la Colma di Craveggia
M29b - la Colma di Craveggia - la Colla
M35 - Zornasco - Alpe Fontana Verde
r.description: Initially very steep path once you reach the ridge follow it with easier slopes. A small stretch at altitude 1147 on a steep slope on the north side requires attention. The last stretch from altitude 1410 to Alpe Fontana Verde is suitable for tourists

r.name: X14 - Alpe Busarasca - Bocchetta di Campo
r.description: A wild path in one of the most remote areas of Val Pogallo, following a non-existent track, looking for obligatory passages, walking on very steep meadows are a constant throughout the entire route

r.name: A51c - loc.tà Coloria, bivio A00a - Trogo - Colletto - Costa dell'Oraccio, bivio A51A
G06 - Verampio - Aleccio
r.description: Steep mule track that from the footbridge on the Marmite dei Giganti leads first to Crego and then to Aleccio

r.name: G34 - Verampio - Premia
r.description: Dirt road that climbs from Verampio to Premia along the entrances to the Marmitte dei Giganti and the Gorges of the area

r.name: A53d - ul Dric, Paset Cesar, bivio A53 (fontana) - Alpe Basciumo sopra, bivio C01
F01b - S. Giovanni - Alpe Bogo
r.description: beginning of the high route of the Divedro valley. Panoramic trail with well-kept mountain pastures. The start takes place on the road to the quarry

r.name: P22 - Ponte Val Gabbio - Bocchetta dell'Usciolo
P20 - Bivio P18 sopra In La Piana - Passo del Ragozzale
P20a - Bivio P20 sopra Alpe Curtin - Passo di Basagrana
P18 - Alpe in la Piana - Bocchetta di Vald

r.description: driveway, with several stretches of asphalt

r.name: P15 - Cicogna - Cima Selva
r.description: Ancient paved mule track that climbs steeply to the Cappelletta di Cima Selva, used before the construction of the valley floor mule track to reach Pogallo, along the route there are many terraces and a lime kiln

r.name: S99 Bocchetta di Cortechiuso - Monte Zeda
M51- Bagni di Craveggia - Bocchetta del Ragozzo
M47 - Alpe Cortaccio - Laghetti dei Muini
M49 - Bivio M51 - Alpe di Ruggia
D03 - Domodossola - Alpe Lusentino
r.description: Also known as "Via del Moncucco" the route from Domodossola leads to the Lusentino alp through the localities of Maggianico and Prata, along the way it is possible to appreciate the beautiful press of Vagna and the farm in Prata

r.name: D01 - Cappella di Marisch - Moncucco
r.description: From the Marish Chapel through the woods you reach Vallesone, cross the asphalt road and take the wide path that leads to Alpe Lusentino, then along the tracks and paths near the sky slopes you reach Alpe Torcelli and shortly after the final crest.

r.name: A51a - Moiachina - Alpe Propiano superiore
r.description: Alternative route to the mountain pastures of Propiano from Piedimulera but also from Pallanzeno with the variant A51d

r.name: L03 - Ponte Faugiol - Cappella della Croce
G00 - Via del Gries da Crevoladossola a Baceno (prima sezione)
r.description: The route follows beautiful mule tracks, a stretch of dirt track after Pontemaglio and village streets within the hamlets

r.name: M53 - Fondo Isorno - B.ta di Medaro
L02 - Cippata - Forcola di Larecchio
r.description: A long, challenging route for experienced hikers, featuring exposed sections and rarely traveled paths. Mixed forests of ancient chestnut trees and beautiful beech woods give way to old alpine pastures and high-altitude meadows.

r.name: L97 - Il Campo - Forcola di Larecchio
L04 - Alpe Cortone - Lago di Larecchio
r.description: A clearly visible route connecting Alpe Cortone to Lake Larecchio via a wide path featuring paved fords and two bridges, the second of which has a metal-grate deck.

r.name: G04 - Crodo - Passo della Forcoletta
r.description: Route from Altoggio onwards on an interesting historical mule track still used by herds heading to Alpe Cravariola, unfortunately the road to Altoggio is private and it is recommended to combine it with an (electric) bike to enjoy the trip

r.name: G02 - Crodo - Alpe Larone
r.description: From Crodo to La Balmella marked and practicable, up to Alpe Moncrovino difficult unmarked path, beyond Moncrovino there is no trace and it is practically impassable

r.name: G30 - Cagiogno - Aleccio
r.description: From Cagiogno, by mule track, to the beautiful Bee mountain pasture from which, by a path that is exposed at times on the hillside, you reach the Aloro mountain pasture. Following a forest road, you reach the equipped area of Piana di Aleccio

r.name: L98 - Rifugio Sironi - Passo della Fria - Confine Svizzero
L99 - Rifugio Sironi - Bocchetta del Lago Gelato
G36 - Crego - Maglioggio
r.description: Easy flat path, for a long stretch you walk on a covered canal, but which for a short slippery stretch and with chains cannot be classified as tourist

r.name: G38 - Cruppo - Crego
r.description: From Cruppo a paved mule track climbs to Dugno then the path climbs very steeply until it reaches the Aleccio road, and then continues on asphalt to Crego

r.name: H01 - Baceno - Cravegna - Deccia - Bta di Deccia
r.description: Very long and tiring journey. As there are roads, it is advisable to reach Deccia starting from Foppiano (the Deccia road has a barrier) following the G09 up to Prepiana (Voma) from where you reach the Deccia road to the right

r.name: A01a - Gaggio - Sogno
r.description: Easy and panoramic path that crosses some hamlets of Villadossola on the eastern side of Moncucco until reaching Sogno

r.name: Variante lungo fiume e bosco Tenso
P50 - Ponte Velina - in La Piana (Ferrata Selvaggio Verde)
r.description: Path of all the low Valgrande: long and challenging physically, recently facilitated by the creation of the Via Ferrata Selvaggio Verde. It can be broken in two days at the Orfalecchio bivac or at the Arca cave

r.name: XA48 - Bettola - Strada Cadorna - Alpe Corte - Bta di Saltir
r.description: From Bettola along one of the many military roads Cadorna to Alpe Corte and then into the wild nature to the Bta di Saltir (or also Sauti)
